This press release is an official information document of the VINCI Group. 1
Nanterre,22 October 2026
FURTHER GROWTH IN REVENUE AND ORDER INTAKE
◼ Strong revenue increase in the third quarter: up 5%, driven by business outside France and
Energy Solutions
◼ Robust order intake; satisfactory order book renewal rate
◼ Very solid financial position
◼ 2026 guidance confirmed, excluding the impact of a possible increase inthe TEITLD1, currently being
reviewed by the French parliament

PRESS RELEASE

This press release is an official information document of the VINCI Group. 2
The changes set out below arerelative to the first nine months of 2025 or the third quarter of 2025 unless otherwise
stated.
I. GOOD OVERALL PERFORMANCE DRIVEN BY BUSINESS OUTSIDE FRANCE AND ENERGY SOLUTIONS
FURTHER REVENUE GROWTH
Consolidated revenue in the third quarter grew strongly by 5% (after remaining stable in the first quarter
and rising by 4% in the second quarter), with revenue outside France up 10%.
In the first nine months of 2026, consolidated revenue thus totalled €56.0 billion, a 3.1% rise comprising
organic growth of 1.8%, a 1.6% positive impact from changes in scope3 and a negative currency effect of
0.2%. It should be noted that:
- this increase was driven by good momentum at Energy Solutions (up 7.4%);
- revenue outside France rose by 6.7% (including a 4.4% increase on a like- for- like basis), accounting
for 60% of the total, compared with 58% in the first nine months of 2025.
ROBUST ORDER INTAKE AND HIGH ORDER BOOK
Order intake at Energy Solutions and VINCI Construction totalled €49.6 billion at 30 September 2026, a
noteworthyincrease of 6%.4
This leads to a satisfactory renewal rate for theorder book, with order intake well above revenue generated
by these business lines in the first nine months of the year (€46.2 billion). At 30 September 2026, the order
book reached the high level of €75.4 billion, up 7% year on year.
It represents 14 months of average business activity for VINCI Energies, Cobra IS and VINCI Construction,
offering visibility to the Group. International business made up 71% of the order book (70% at 30September
2025).
VERY SOLID FINANCIAL POSITION
VINCI’s consolidated net financial debt at 30 September 2026 amounted to€20.2 billion, down €1.2 billion
year on year.
VINCI’s liquidity position remains very strong:
- €14.7 billion of net cash managed;
- a €6.5 billion confirmed and unused credit facility5 at VINCI SA.
Supported by its high - quality order book and its very solid financial position, the Group looks to the
future with serenity.
3 Changes mainly consisted of the following: (i) in the Concessions business, the full consolidation of the Brazilian highway concession holder
Entrevias since October 2025(revenue of €106 million in the first nine months of 2026) at VINCI Highways; the end of the concession contract for
Phnom Penh airport in Cambodia at VINCI Airports in September 2025 (see details on the following page); the end of the concession contract for the
Stade de France in August 2025 at VINCI Stadium (which had made a revenue contribution of around €60 million in 2025); (ii) at VINCI Energies,
23 acquisitions in the first nine months of 2026 and 33 acquisitions in 2025, which contributed€530 million to the increase in revenue in the period;
(iii) at VINCI Construction, more than €375 million of additional revenue, of which nearly €170 million for Fletcher Construction in New Zealand
(acquisition completed at end-May 2026).
4 Including a 6% rise also in flow business, which accounts for the majority of revenue for the Energy Solutions and Construction businesses.
5 Due to expire in January 2031.

This press release is an official information document of the VINCI Group. 3
II. KEY HIGHLIGHTS BY BUSINESS
CONCESSIONS
Revenue in the Concessions business amounted to €9.6 billion, up 1.8% on an actual basis (up 2.4% like-
for- like) despite an unfavourable economic environment. This performance reflects the good
diversification of its portfolio of airport and motorway assets and their resilience to headwinds.
• VINCI Airports
VINCI Airports’ passenger numbers remained stable despite high prices for kerosene and geopolitical
disruptions, with 253 million passengers welcomed across the airports managed by the Group in the first
nine months of 2026.6 Solid growth at a number of airports (particularly Edinburgh, Belgrade and Budapest
as well as the network’s airports in Portugal, CaboVerde and the Dominican Republic) offset the weakness
noted at London Gatwick and in Asia.
Nevertheless, revenue at VINCI Airports rose by2.8% on an actual basis (including a 4.2% rise in the third
quarter) to €3.8 billion, despite negative scope effects 7. On a like - for- like basis, it grew by 5.0%. This
performance demonstrates the ability of the division to optimise both aviation and non- aviation activities,
in particular by passing on inflation.
• VINCI Autoroutes
In the first nine months of 2026,traffic levels across all vehicle types fell by 3.3%. Light vehicle traffic was
down 4.0%, primarily due to surging fuel prices . Meanwhile, heavy vehicle traffic continued to show a
positive trend (up 1.2%).
This good momentum for heavy vehicle traffic partially accounts for the relatively limited decline in revenue
recorded by VINCI Autoroutes (down 0.8% to €5.1 billion).
• VINCI Highways
Buoyed by the addition of Brazilian highways to the portfolio,8 revenue saw a strong increase of 40% on an
actual basis (up 10% like- for- like) to €528 million.
6 Figures at 100% including passenger numbers at all managed airports over the period as a whole.
7 The previous international airport in Phnom Penh (Cambodia), which was operated by VINCI Airports subsidiary Cambodia Airport s under a
concession contract, closed in early September 2025. Since then, Cambodia Airports has held an operating contract for Phnom Pe nh’s new
international airport (Techo International). Overall, Cambodia Airports generated revenue of €29 million in the first nine months of 2026, as opposed
to €119 million in the first nine months of 2025.
8 As a reminder, apart from Entrevias (see previous page), VINCI Highways took over operation– under a new concession– of Via Cristais in Brazil in
March 2025 (€66 million of revenue in the first nine months of 2026 and €47 million of revenue in the first nine months of 2025).

This press release is an official information document of the VINCI Group. 4
ENERGY SOLUTIONS
VINCI’s Energy Solutions business operates in buoyant markets: increasing shift towards electrification,
growth for AI and data centres, digital infrastructure services, optimisation of industrial processes and
building performance, defence and sovereigntychallenges.
Shaped by these powerful megatrends, the main indicators relating to this business in the first nine
months of 2026 were very well oriented. Highlights included:
- revenue growth (up 7.4% to €22.3 billion, 70% of which was generated outside France), with
strong growth in the third quarter (up 8.6%);
- increases in order intake (up 9% to €24.3 billion) and the order book (up 9% year on year to
€38.5 billion);
- VINCI Energies’ active acquisition policy in fragmented markets.
• VINCI Energies
Revenue rose by 8.2% in the third quarter (up 4.2% like - for- like). In the first nine months of 2026, it
amounted to €16.4 billion, an increase of 7.2% (up 3.7% like - for- like). This performance reflects the
dynamism of the business line’s companies in robust markets, both in France (up 5.2%) and internationally
(up 8.5%, including a 12% increase in Germany, to €2.9 billion). Revenue generated outside France
accounted for 60% of the total.
Order intake was up 8% to €18.5 billion9 and was appreciably higher than revenue in the first nine months
of 2026. It also hit a new rolling 12- month record ofnearly €24 billion.
VINCI Energies’ order book at 30 September 2026 amounted to €20.2 billion, up 11% year on year, and
represents 11 months of the business line’s average business activity.
• Cobra IS
Revenue rose by 9.7% in the third quarter. In the first nine months of 2026, it rose by 8.0% to €5.8 billion.
This growth was driven in particular by flow business (60% of total revenue), which remains verystrong in
Spain.
Order intake in the first nine months of 2026 rose by 11% to €5.8 billion, due to the many contracts for
projects of varying sizes won in the third quarter.10
Cobra IS’s order book at 30 September 2026 amounted to €18.3 billion, up 6% year on year. It represents
more than two years of the business line’s average business activity.
9 The main contracts won by VINCI Energies in the third quarter included technical works packages for a data centrein Indonesia, a high-tech clean
room for semiconductor R&D in Singaporeand the renovation of power lines in Germany and the United Kingdom.
10 The main contracts won by Cobra IS in the third quarter included theconstruction of a solar plant in Mexico,the installation of a cooling system
for a data centre campus located in the Iberian Peninsula (see the VINCI press release dated20 October 2026), the installation of synchronisers on
the Spanish grid, a further phase of electromechanical works for a data centre in Spainand the renovation/ maintenance of public lighting systems
in Huelva (Spain).

This press release is an official information document of the VINCI Group. 5
CONSTRUCTION
In the Construction business, revenue reached a high level (€24.6 billion). Highlights include d good
momentum outside France for both Proximity Networks and Specialty Networks and the successful
integration of the New Zealand public works company Fletcher Construction.
• VINCI Construction
Buoyed by dynamic activity outside France in the third quarter,11 revenue totalled €23.9 billion in the first
nine months of 2026 (up 0.8% actual and down 0.2% like- for- like).
In line with the trend observed in previous quarters, key points were:
- lower business levels for Major Projects (representing less than 10% of the total revenue of
VINCI Construction), due in particular to progress on the High Speed 2 line in the United Kingdom;
- a decline in revenue in France, as a c onsequence of the usual electoral cycles,12 and phasing
effects for some building projects;
- a favourable revenue trend at the business line’s other divisions, particularly Oceania,
Central Europe and the United Kingdom.
Order intake in the first nine months of 2026 rose by 3% to €25.3 billion13 and was higher than revenue in
the period.
VINCI Construction’s order book at 30 September 2026 amounted to €36.9 billion, up 5% year on year.
It represents 14 months of the business line’s average business activity.
• VINCI Immobilier
In a property development market still facing very challenging conditions, VINCI Immobilier’s revenue was
down 14% to €630 million.
Against this backdrop, the number of reservations in France fell by 23% to 2,313 residential units.
11 Up 11% actual and up 6% like-for-like.
12 Municipal elections were held in March 2026.
13 The main contracts won by VINCI Construction in the third quarter included the extension of the T7 tram line in the Paris region, multi-year road
services in Greater London, roadworks in Australia and the construction of a conference centrein Southport (United Kingdom).

This press release is an official information document of the VINCI Group. 6
III. OTHER HIGHLIGHTS
MAIN RECENT DEVELOPMENTS
• Energy Solutions
VINCI Energies completed the acquisitions of 23 new companies in the first nine months of 2026,
representing combined annual revenue of around €220 million, mainly outside France (in the Benelux
countries, the United Kingdom, North America, Australia and New Zealand).
Furthermore, on 13 October 2026, VINCI Energies completed the acquisition of the German company
All for One, a specialist in the integration and maintenance of business applications having generated
revenue of €500 million in 2025, with a workforce of around 3,000 highly skilled employees.
This acquisition gives VINCI Energies a stronger presence and further supports its ambitions, through its
Axians brand, in the fast -growing digital infrastructure services market (business applications, cloud
services, data analytics and AI). It will allow Axians to seize the many opportunities created by the
acceleration of digital transformation in Europe.
In July, Cobra IS sold its 50% stake in the Brazilian company Pampa, which holds the public -private
partnership (PPP) contract for the high- voltage transmission line project of the same name. Cobra IS will
continue to operate and maintain the Pampa transmissionline.
This transaction is a fine illustration of Cobra IS’s expertise in carrying out major high- voltage transmission
line projects (such as currently in Brazil and Australia) and in optimising the management of its asset
portfolio.
Since 2023 in Brazil, Cobra IS has also sold its 50% stakes in the Mantiqueira Transmissora, Sertanejaand
Chimarrao PPPs. The four disposals have generated proceedsof more than €300 million.
SHAREHOLDER REMUNERATION
The Group carried out share buy- backs in the total amount of €1.7 billion in the first nine months of 2026
(13.7 million shares bought back at an average price of €122.5).14
On 1 October 2026, VINCI implemented a new share buy -back programme with a maximum purchase
amount of €270 million to be completed by 21 December 2026.
14 As a reminder, the Group carried out share buy-backs in the total amount of €1.4 billion in the first nine months of 2025 (12.1 million shares bought
back at an average price of €119.4).

This press release is an official information document of the VINCI Group. 7
IV. 2026 GUIDANCE CONFIRMED AT CONSTANT TAXATION
Given the excellent financial performance noted since the start of the year, VINCI confirms its 2026
guidance, which anticipates:
o further growth inits revenue, operating earnings and net income attributable to owners of
the parent;
o free cash flow that could reach €6 billion.15
This guidance does not factor in the adverse impact of a possible increase in France’s tax on long- distance
transport infrastructure operators (mainly those operating motorways), which is currently being reviewed by
the French parliament.16
As an initial estimate, the potential accounting impact of such a measure on VINCI’s operating earnings and
net profit attributable to owners of the parent in 2026 would be an additional charge of around €450 million,
to be paid in 2027.
15 Assuming that Zero.e’s capex is similar to its 2025 level (€0.9 billion).
16 Article 22 of France’s 2027 Finance Bill presented to the French parliament proposes “an increase in the long-distance transport infrastructure
tax for the most profitable operators”.

This press release is an official information document of the VINCI Group. 8

GLOSSARY
Concession subsidiaries’ revenue derived from works carried out by non- Group companies: this indicator relates to
construction work done by concession companies as programme manager on behalf of concession grantors.
Consideration for that work is recognised as an intangible asset or financial asset depending on the accounting model
applied to the concession contract, in accordance with IFRIC 12 “Service Concession Arrangements”. It excludes work
done by the VINCI Energies, Cobra IS and VINCI Construction business lines.
Like- for- like revenue growth:this indicator measures the change in revenue at constant scope and exchange rates.
• Constant scope: the scope effect is neutralised as follows:
o For revenue in year Y, revenue from companies that joined the Group in year Y is deducted.
o For revenue in year Y−1, the full - year revenue of companies that joined the Group in year Y−1 is
included, and revenue from companies that left the Group in years Y−1 and Y is excluded.
• Constant exchange rates: the currency effect is neutralised by applying exchange rates in year Y to foreign
currency revenue in year Y−1.
Net financial surplus/debt:this corresponds to the difference between financial assets and financial debt. If the assets
outweigh the liabilities, the balance represents a net financial surplus, and if the liabilities outweigh the assets, the
balance represents net financial debt. Financial debt includes bonds, bank borrowings and debt owed to financial
institutions (including derivatives and other liabilities relating to hedging instruments). Financial assets include cash
and cash equivalents and assets relating to derivative instruments.
Under IFRS 16, the Group recognises right- of- use assets relating to leased items under non- current assets, along with
a liability corresponding to the present value of lease payments still to be made. That liability is not included in net
financial surplus/debt as defined by the Group, and is presented directly on the balance sheet.
Order book:
• At VINCI Energies, Cobra IS and VINCI Construction, the order book represents the volume of business yet to be
carried out on projects where the contract is in force (in particular after service orders have been obtained or after
conditions precedent havebeen met) and financed.
• At VINCI Immobilier, the order book corresponds to the revenue, recognised on a progress- towards- completion

with respect to property development contracts on which the works order has been given by the project owner.
Order intake:
• At VINCI Energies, Cobra IS and VINCI Construction, a new order is recorded when the contract has been not only
signed but is also in force (for example, after the service order has been obtained or after conditions precedent
have been met) and when the project’s financing is in place. The amount recorded in order intake corresponds to
the contractual revenue.
• At VINCI Immobilier, order intake(reservations)corresponds to the value of properties sold off- plan or sold after
completion in accordance with a notarised deed, or revenue from property development contracts where the works
order has been given by the project owner.
For joint property developments:
o If VINCI Immobilier has sole control over the development company, it is fully consolidated. In that case,
100% of the contract value is included in order intake.
o If the development company is jointly controlled, it is accounted for under the equity method and its
order intake is not included in the total.
VINCI Airports’ passenger numbers: this is the number of passengers who have travelled on commercial flights from
or to a VINCI Airports airport during a given period, and is a relevant indicator for estimating an airport’s revenue from
both aviation and non- aviation activities.
VINCI Autoroutes’ traffic levels:this is the number of kilometres travelled by light and heavy vehicles on the motorway
network managed by VINCI Autoroutes during a given period.
